camera.model: FLIR Blackfly S BFS-U3-51S5PC (Sony on-chip 0/45/90/135 deg polarizers, RGB)

demosaicing: polanalyser as is: pa.demosaicing(COLOR_PolarRGB) (bilinear) -> pa.calcStokes(0/45/90/135 deg); S3 = 0
stokes_frame: angle measured from image x (right) increasing toward image UP (= main.py measurement frame, e2 ~ -y_cam); light direction = incident; mount roll 90 deg handled by rvec (R_c2w) in main.py for both cameras

evidence.method: same linear polarizing film shot with FLIR and Basler (reference: Basler pcalib), horizontal and tilted
evidence.conclusion: S1 and S2 signs agree with offset 0 deg (offset 90 deg flips both). ~2 deg difference = roll difference between the two mounts.
independent_checks: floor specular reflection in FLIR/test/20261007/201956 is s-polarized (horizontal) only with offset 0
lens-front ND radial false polarization (radiometric/nd/data/20261008/201539) matches theory only with angles increasing toward image up

known_limitations.dolp_of_film: FLIR 0.80-0.89 vs Basler 0.96-1.0 on the same film -> on-chip polarizer extinction ratio limit; not corrected
known_limitations.aperture: sky DoLP drops ~4% from f/11 to f/4 (10/14: 0.335 / 0.329 / 0.322) -> possibly extinction ratio vs cone angle; check at f/4
known_limitations.status: angle reference only; no extinction-ratio / per-pixel polarimetric calibration (user: probably not needed with bilinear demosaicing)

data.notes_md: repo capture/memo.md (FLIR polarization convention confirmed on 2026-10-08)

history: captured and decided 2026-10-08; moved from FLIR/before/test/20261008 on 2026-10-15
